subject: End-of-day vs UTC boundary for SOC2 Type II — clarifying partial-month migration window
body:
From: Alice Ramirez <alice.ramirez@thirdbridge-audit.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Security <PlatformSecurity@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II window — weekend migration and partial-month evidence question

Hi Soojin / Karthik,

Quick question from the audit team for Acme's Type II testing: their infrastructure migration happened over a weekend that straddled the end of August (started 2026-08-29 22:30 PDT, finished 2026-08-30 03:15 PDT). The auditor is trying to understand whether your evidence (logs, access control snapshots) should be treated as belonging to the August reporting period or the September period. Specifically: do your SOC 2 controls treat an "end-of-day" boundary as local server-time end of day, or as UTC 00:00?

They also asked whether Redwood can provide a short bridge letter that states the snapshot semantics for any point-in-time evidence that falls on that weekend, and confirm which days you consider fully inclusive for the August Type II coverage.

Can you confirm:
- Which timezone semantics you use for point-in-time snapshots and log cutoffs tied to an audit period
- Whether events recorded between 2026-08-29 22:30 PDT and 2026-08-30 03:15 PDT count toward August evidence or September for your SOC 2 Type II reporting
- If you can produce a one-page bridge letter we can include in the working papers (PDF okay)

Appreciate a short answer so we can advance the testing plan this week.

Thanks,
Alice Ramirez
Senior Auditor | ThirdBridge Audit Services

----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramirez <alice.ramirez@thirdbridge-audit.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Platform Security <PlatformSecurity@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II window — weekend migration and partial-month evidence question

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front, details below:

- Snapshot/log cutoff semantics: UTC 00:00 is the canonical boundary for audit evidence we provide; we normalize server logs to UTC for SOC 2 artifacts.
- Events in your timeframe (2026-08-29 22:30 PDT — 2026-08-30 03:15 PDT) are treated as August evidence in our Type II reporting because they occurred before 2026-09-01 00:00:00 UTC.
- We can provide a one-page bridge letter confirming the snapshot semantics and the migration window; attaching a draft and a CSV sample of the point-in-time log excerpt for the timeframe you cited.

Notes/context: our ingestion pipeline records events with a UTC timestamp and our daily rollovers for the audit pipeline are performed at UTC midnight. For convenience we sometimes show local times in operational dashboards, but every artifact we deliver for SOC 2 (log extracts, config snapshots, access lists) will reference UTC.

Action items:
- I attached a draft bridge letter (PDF) and a tiny CSV with a sample of the log rows around the migration window. Please confirm wording for the bridge letter and if you need the full-day extracts instead of the sample.
- Karthik: can you confirm the retention cutover/replication note mentioned below so I can add one sentence to the bridge letter about replication lag guarantees?

S — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_bridge_letter_20260831.pdf (application/pdf), evidence_point_in_time_log_sample.csv (text/csv)

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alice Ramirez <alice.ramirez@thirdbridge-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Platform Security <PlatformSecurity@acmeinc.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II window — weekend migration and partial-month evidence question

Following up with the replication detail for the bridge letter: our secondary replica in us-west-2 receives writes within 90 seconds under normal load and we have an automated checkpoint every 10 minutes. For audit evidence we preserve the primary timeline and include replica metadata showing commit timestamps (all in UTC). There were no retention policy changes around 2026-08-29/30.

I also confirmed that the maintenance migration did not involve any asynchronous buffering that would reassign event timestamps — the services used preserved original event timestamps and we did not backdate or rewrite entries during the migration.

Marissa, tagging you since you own the contract language with Acme; anything you want to add for the auditor or to the bridge letter?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramirez <alice.ramirez@thirdbridge-audit.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II window — weekend migration and partial-month evidence question

Alice — this looks good from a contracts perspective. The only note I would add is that for the bridge letter we should avoid firm commitments that change contractual SLA terms; suggest we phrase the replication timing as "typical observed replication latency" and reference the attached sample log rather than promising a specific RPO.

If that language works for ThirdBridge I'll ask Legal to do a quick review and then we can DocuSign the bridge letter.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

----
